title: Debug binary search off-by-one bug — 3 turns
description: Binary search implementation has an off-by-one bug causing infinite loop. Tests fail. Multi-turn: fix the bug, verify edge cases, confirm all tests pass.

task_spec.prompt: The `binary_search` function in `binary_search.py` has an off-by-one bug — when `arr[mid] < target`, it sets `low = mid` instead of `low = mid + 1`, which can cause an infinite loop. Fix `binary_search()` so the tests pass. Run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` to check.
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` to check the current state. Walk me through the fixes you made. If any tests are still failing — especially the edge cases (empty list, single element) — show me the errors and fix them. Also look at `search_range()` — it has the same family of bugs in its find_left and find_right helpers.
Final verification: run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` and confirm a completely clean build. Every test must pass — fix anything still red now.
success_criteria: binary_search has no infinite loop (low = mid + 1 when arr[mid] < target)
Single element works for found and not-found
search_range correctly finds first and last index of duplicates
